headline: Northwind Energy posts record quarter as offshore wind output surges
subheadline: Revenue rose 23% year on year, though the company warned of supply-chain pressure on turbine components.
description: Northwind Energy reported record quarterly revenue, up 23%, driven by a surge in offshore wind output, while warning about supply-chain pressures on turbine components.
author: j-okafor

image.caption: An offshore wind farm (file photo). Northwind's Greyshoal array came fully online in the third quarter.

seo.title: Northwind Energy posts record quarter on offshore wind surge
seo.description: Northwind Energy's revenue rose 23% to a quarterly record as offshore wind output surged; the company flagged turbine supply-chain pressure.

body: AURELIA CITY — Northwind Energy reported its strongest quarter on record on Wednesday, with revenue up 23% to €2.9bn as its Greyshoal offshore array reached full capacity three months ahead of schedule.
Operating profit rose 31%, beating analyst expectations, and the company raised its full-year guidance. Shares rose 6% in early trading before settling 4% higher.

Chief executive remarks accompanying the results struck a more cautious note on 2027, warning that lead times for gearboxes and large castings had lengthened and that two planned projects could slip by up to a year.

body.text: Demand is not our problem. Getting steel, bearings and vessels in the right place at the right time is.

body: Analysts said the results confirmed a broader trend of offshore wind operators outperforming as power-purchase agreements signed during the 2022–2024 price spike begin to deliver. Several noted that Northwind's hedging programme had protected it from this year's softer wholesale prices.

The company will pay an interim dividend of €0.18 per share. It also confirmed it is in early talks to supply electricity to a planned sea-wall and pumping programme under the new Coastal Cities Alliance flood-defence fund.
